crossCuttingThemes.label: Regional sphere
crossCuttingThemes.description: Draw a geographic line—Americas, Middle East, Persian Gulf—and treat crossing it as a threat to U.S. peace or vital interests.

crossCuttingThemes.label: Anti-communism & containment
crossCuttingThemes.description: From Truman through Reagan, doctrines name communist expansion (often Soviet-linked) as the core threat and promise aid or force to stop it.

crossCuttingThemes.label: Intervention thresholds
crossCuttingThemes.description: When revolutions, aggression, or instability cross a line—communist takeovers, outside control of oil routes, genocide—the U.S. claims a right to act.

crossCuttingThemes.label: Burden-sharing & allies
crossCuttingThemes.description: Nixon expects partners to supply manpower; later presidents press allies on costs (Trump) or consult before fighting (Biden).

crossCuttingThemes.label: Aid, proxies, and force
crossCuttingThemes.description: Military/economic assistance, regional “police” roles, and proxy insurgents appear before—or instead of—large U.S. ground wars.
